J.S KLAR, PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER :-
By this common order, we intend to dispose of the above

referred two first appeals, as they have arisen out of the same order

dated 29.10.2014 of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal

Forum, Ferozepur (in short the 'District Forum), as such, they can be

disposed of together. The order shall be pronounced by us in main

first appeal no.37 of 2015 titled as "HCL Infosystems Limited Vs.

Vishal Arora & another", which has been filed by opposite party

no.1 against above order, vide which, the complaint of complainant

was accepted by directing OPs to refund Rs.15,800/- as sale price of

the mobile handset alongwith interest @9% per annum from the date
First Appeal No.37 of 2015 3
of its purchase i.e. 13.07.2012 till realization; further to pay Rs.3000/-

as compensation for harassment and Rs.2000/- as litigation

expenses jointly and severally. The appellant of this appeal is OP

No.1 and respondent no.1 of this appeal is complainant and

respondent no.2 of this appeal is opposite party no.2 before the

District Forum in the original complaint and they be referred as such

hereinafter for the sake of convenience.
2. First appeal no.167 of 2015 has been filed by opposite

party no.2 now appellant against order dated 29.10.2014 of the

District Forum. The appellant of this appeal is OP no.2, respondent

no.1 of this appeal is complainant and respondent no.2 of this appeal

is OP no.1 in the complaint before the District Forum and they be

referred as such hereinafter for the sake of convenience.
3. Complainant Vishal Arora filed complaint under
Section

12
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (in short, "the Act") against

the OPs on the averments that on 13.07.2012, he purchased mobile

phone Blackberry 9380 curve(Black) bearing IMEI

No.359598044098796 from OP no.2 against price of Rs.15,800/-,

manufactured by OP no.1. It was assured by OPs that mobile phone

carried warranty of half year. The complainant noticed some

problems of restart i.e. power off and on automatically, not catching

the network, handing and charging with the said phone. When

approached by complainant, OP no.2 told that software of blackberry

needed to be reloaded into the mobile set and it required back up

and the said problems would be removed by doing the back up of
First Appeal No.37 of 2015 4
the mobile phone. OP no.2 copied all the data and mobile numbers

of the mobile of the complainant in the pen drive of complainant and

asked him to collect the mobile in the evening. OP no.2 had not

issued any job sheet on the pretext that stationery was out of stock

and the same was ordered with the printing press for printing. The

complainant visited OP no.2 in the evening and the mobile phone

was handed over to him on the assurance that it became defect free.
He found that the problems still persisted in the mobile set and it was

rendered useless. The complainant was intimated that there was

manufacturing defect in the mobile phone set, which became

unrepairable. The complainant pleaded that above said defects

occurred in the mobile set during the warranty period. The

complainant prayed that OPs be directed to refund the price of

Rs.15,800/- alongwith interest @12% per annum from the date of its

purchase till realization; further to pay Rs.20,000/- as compensation

for mental pain; and to pay Rs.11,000/- as litigation expenses.
4. Upon notice, OPs did not put in appearance and were set

ex-parte before the District Forum.
5. The complainant tendered in ex-parte evidence affidavits

and documents Ex.C-1 to C-16 and closed the evidence. On

conclusion of ex-parte evidence and arguments, the District Forum

accepted the complaint of the complainant, as referred to above.

Aggrieved by ex-parte order of the District Forum, the above referred

two appeals have been preferred against the same by the OPs.
First Appeal No.37 of 2015 5
6. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and

have also examined the record of the case. Firstly, on the point of

setting the OPs now appellants ex-parte before the District Forum

below, we find that the District Forum sent the notices to OPs

through registered post and OP no.2 had not appeared despite

service and was set ex-parte on 20.06.2014. OP no.1 was set ex-

parte by the District Forum, vide order dated 19.09.2014. Even OP

no.1 applied for setting aside the ex-parte order of the District Forum

and this application of OP no.1 was declined by the District Forum

vide order dated 27.10.2014. We don't find any flaw in the order of

the District Forum in setting OPs ex-parte, who are the present

appellants in the above appeals.
7. Now, we proceed to settle the controversy in this case on

merits, raging between the parties. The pleadings of the complainant

have been carefully examined by us. He filed his affidavit Ex.C-1 on

the record to the effect that he purchased mobile set from OP no.2,

which was manufactured by OP no.1 for price of Rs.15,800/- on

13.07.2012. He further deposed that mobile set carried warranty of

six months period and it started giving recurrent problems during the

above period of warranty. He further deposed that he contacted OPs

in this regard and they told that software of blackberry needed to be

reloaded. This witness further stated that due lack of stationery, OP

no.2 did not issue any job sheet. The complainant further testified

that the problems in the mobile set still persisted, after its repair for

which he raised grievance with OPs. The complainant stated in his
First Appeal No.37 of 2015 6
affidavit on oath that defect in the mobile set developed during the

warranty period and he wanted refund of the price of mobile set with

interest. Ex.C-2 is the receipt for purchase of mobile set in question

for Rs.15,800/- on 13.07.2012 from OP no.2. Legal notice served

upon OPs is Ex.C-4. Ex.C-6 is the status report of the mobile set of

Blackberry curve 9380 as discontinued. The report of Hemant Sony,

mobile repairer is Ex.C-8 on the record and his affidavit is Ex.C-9.

This witness has testified in his affidavit that he submitted this report

Ex.C-8. He further stated that the mobile set purchased by the

complainant has manufacturing problem, because he examined it

continuously for a period of two years for repair purposes. He stated

that there was network problem in it. There was also problem of

charging in the mobile set. He further testified that the mobile set has

become unrepairable. Ex.C-10 is the guidelines issued by HCL touch

support & services. Ex.C-11 is the order of the District Forum dated

12.12.2012 passed against OPs in the complaint of Sanav Singh.

Ex.C-12 is the application for execution proceedings under
Section

27
of Consumer Protection Act. Ex.C-13 has further shown that

warrant of arrest were issued against OPs in execution application/

proceeding in case of Sanav Singh. Ex.C-14 and C-15 are the zimni

orders passed by the Forum therein. Ex.C-16 is the supplementary

affidavit of complainant. We find that above referred evidence has

gone unrebutted on the record. There is no rebuttal evidence

adduced by the OPs in this case to the above evidence of the

complainant, because they were set ex-parte.
First Appeal No.37 of 2015 7
8. It is, thus, proved fact that complainant purchased the

mobile set from OP no.2, manufactured by OP no.1 for price. The

complainant is consumer of OPs. The mobile set gave the recurrent

problems after its purchase during warranty period. Presumptive

warranty is there just after sale of new mobile set by OP no.2 to

complainant. The mobile set was rendered defective during the

warranty period and it was not made faultless by OPs, when taken to

OPs by the complainant. Even the report of Hemant Sony Ex.C-8

duly supported by his affidavit Ex.C-9 is on the record lending

corroboration to the case of the complainant that there was

manufacturing defect in the mobile set. We find that the order of the

District Forum suffers from no illegality or material infirmity in this

case.
Consumer Protection Act
is consumer orientated Act and it has

been designed by the legislature with the sole purpose to protect the

innocent consumers from their exploitation by big business houses.

We are in agreement with the finding of the District Forum holding

the OPs deficient in service jointly and severally. The order of the

District Forum Ferozepur under challenge in the above referred

appeals is, thus, affirmed in these appeals.
9. As a result of our above discussion, we find no merit in

first appeal no.37 of 2015 and first appeal no.167 of 2015 and both

the above appeals are hereby dismissed.
10. In First Appeal No.37 of 2015, the appellant had

deposited an amount of Rs.12,165/- in this Commission at the time

of filing the appeal. This amount alongwith interest, which accrued
First Appeal No.37 of 2015 8
thereon, if any, be remitted by the registry to respondent no.1 of this

appeal being complainant by way of crossed cheque/demand draft

after 45 days from receipt of certified copy of this order.
11. In First Appeal No.167 of 2015, the appellant had

deposited an amount of Rs.12,200/- in this Commission at the time

of filing the appeal. After calculating the interest on above amount,

the amount be remitted by the registry to respondent no.1 of this

appeal being complainant, as per his entitlement in a strict manner,

as per this order, by way of crossed cheque/demand draft after 45

days. Remaining amount, if any, be remitted by the registry to

appellant of this appeal.
12. Arguments in above referred appeals were heard on

14.03.2017 and the orders were reserved. Certified copies of the

orders be communicated to the parties as per rules.
13. The appeals could not be decided within the statutory

period due to heavy pendency of court cases.
(J. S. KLAR)
 PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER

 (SURINDER PAL KAUR)
 MEMBER

March 16, 2017
